---PROTOCOL---
# eMicro offline control-plane contract, version 4.0.2

Repair and extend the supplied multi-file compiler and CPU map agent. The evaluated system compiles policies, publishes immutable map images, and replays explicit causal events. It models request identity and observable transport/storage handoffs; it does not run a kernel, deploy services, authenticate peers or infer causality from real traffic.

## Artifact and command

The editable artifact is the **entire `/workspace/project` directory**, including any additional ordinary files you need. Implement its `driver.py`. All files in that directory are collected; no particular internal algorithm, class, module arrangement or coding style is required. The supplied compiler constructs real FAdo automata; the serial export and memory-map loader run on CPU. Their existing behavior is incomplete. The parser/JSON entry skeleton is supplied. In particular, the starter does not implement the required lifecycle, transactions or canonical export, and retains legacy language/empty-language/performance defects.

`python3 /workspace/launch.py` runs `project/driver.py` with the pinned offline packages on its import path, working directory `/workspace/project`. Read one UTF-8 JSON request from stdin, write one JSON response to stdout and exit **0**. JSON key order/whitespace do not matter. Array order, integer values and Boolean types do. Extra stdout, empty/non-JSON output, wrong values or nonzero exit fail. Stderr is diagnostic only. No Python stream interception is used. Text, binary streams and OS descriptors 0/1 all work. Flushed valid output followed by `os._exit(0)` is accepted. Each invocation has fresh system state; jobs are independent.

The request is exactly `{"jobs":[JOB,...]}`. A job has exactly `services`, `limits`, `events`. The response is exactly `{"results":[RESULT,...]}`. A valid job yields `{"events":[OUTCOME,...]}` in event order. Invalid job structure/types/static bounds yield `{"error":"invalid"}` for that job, with no replay. Invalid UTF-8/JSON, duplicate keys, nonfinite numbers, incorrect top-level schema or whole-request bounds yield `{"error":"invalid"}` for the whole request. JSON floating-point tokens are decoded to binary64; a token that overflows to infinity is a whole-request error, while underflow to finite zero is permitted. Finite JSON floats are parsed but never valid for integer fields; Booleans are not integers. Trailing whitespace is allowed; trailing JSON is not. Integer tokens longer than 4300 decimal digits (excluding a leading minus) are whole-request JSON errors. JSON container nesting is limited to 64: each object or array contributes one level, including the outer request object at level 1; strings, including escaped brackets/quotes, contribute none. Exceeding 64 levels is a whole-request `invalid` error before job validation, even when the deep value is in an otherwise invalid job. Up to 64 levels, malformed job contents retain job-level error scope. Malformed JSON and parser failures are whole-request errors, never partial results. A leading UTF-8 BOM is rejected. JSON whitespace outside strings is exactly space U+0020, tab U+0009, LF U+000A and CR U+000D.

`services` is a nonempty list of at most 16 objects exactly `{"name":NAME,"label":LABEL}`. Names match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,23}` and labels are integers 1..4294967294; both are unique. Every image uses columns in **increasing label order**, independent of registry order. `limits` has exactly these keys, each an integer from 1 to the shown maximum:

| key | maximum | resident objects counted |
|---|---:|---|
| images | 16 | staged/active/inactive immutable images |
| cells | 262144 | transitions whose target is not DENY, across resident images |
| units | 1024 | live process identities |
| contexts | 32768 | all live request contexts, including cloned copies |
| connections | 4096 | open connection generations |
| packets | 32768 | sent packets retained until close, including delivered packets |
| files | 8192 | current inode generations |

An event is an object with exactly `op` and the fields listed below. `U` means `[namespace,pid,generation]`, with namespace 0..4294967295 and the other two fields 1..4294967295. `C` and `F` mean `[id,generation]`, both fields 1..4294967295. All epochs, request IDs (`rid`) and stream IDs are integers 1..4294967295. Services/destinations must have the NAME lexical form; an unregistered one is a replay rejection. `policy` is a UTF-8-encodable string; an unpaired surrogate makes that job invalid. There is **no separate per-string byte cap**. The 8 MiB policy-byte budget is exclusively a whole-request sum over structurally valid jobs, including strings whose policy grammar or replay stage is rejected. Thus an otherwise valid job containing one string longer than 8 MiB causes whole-request `invalid`; a structurally invalid job is excluded from that sum. The 24 MiB raw-input cap still includes all jobs and bytes. `wire` is null or a string of at most 96 characters; malformed contents cause a replay rejection. Unknown operations/fields, missing fields and incorrect types make the **job** invalid.

## Policy language and images

A policy string is zero or more `PREDICATE ACTION;` rules; the only ignored whitespace between tokens is space U+0020, tab U+0009, form feed U+000C, CR U+000D and LF U+000A. Vertical tab U+000B and all other Unicode whitespace are forbidden in policy syntax and reject that `stage`; characters within a service name are never ignored. ACTION is `allow` or `drop`. Predicates are `match(PATH)`, `startswith(PATH)`, `endswith(PATH)`, `contains(PATH)`, `(PREDICATE and PREDICATE)`, `(PREDICATE or PREDICATE)` or `not(PREDICATE)`. PATH is a comma-separated sequence of registered names, possibly empty. Parentheses in binary expressions are mandatory. No comments/other syntax is supported. Predicates concern sequences of **services**, not characters. `match` is exact equality; the other three are prefix, suffix and contiguous subsequence. Empty paths match every sequence for those three and only the empty sequence for `match`. Boolean operations have their usual set meanings over every finite sequence of registered services. A sequence is allowed iff at least one allow rule matches and no drop rule matches. No allow rules means the empty language.

Each rule has predicate nesting depth at most 16 (an atom has depth 1), every path has at most 16 services. At most eight rules per string may have a predicate other than a single `match` atom; each such predicate has at most 32 atom occurrences. There are at most four **distinct** non-`match` atoms per string, each with path length at most four. Each string has at most 32768 atom occurrences and 65536 path-service occurrences. Syntax/registry/these policy-bound violations reject that `stage` event. A syntactically valid string satisfying these bounds is counted toward the whole-request atom/path totals even if it names an unregistered service or its stage is later rejected. Invalid strings are not counted toward these two totals.

An image is exactly `{"accept":[BOOL,...],"rows":[[TARGET,...],...]}`. It represents the minimal deterministic complete language machine after removal of its dead residual. Two histories share a label exactly when every possible continuation has the same allowedness. Label 0 is the empty history's residual, called START. Retain only residuals that can reach an allowed sequence, except START is always retained. All other/dead transitions have the integer target **DENY=4294967295**. DENY has no row and remains DENY under every service. Number the retained residuals by breadth-first discovery from START, considering outgoing columns in increasing service-label order and ignoring DENY. `accept[s]` is allowedness of a complete history with label `s`; live-prefix reachability does not imply acceptance. An empty language has one false acceptance flag and one all-DENY row. An all-allow language has one true flag and a row of zeroes. Reject a stage whose resulting image has more than 8192 rows. These are output semantics, not an implementation prescription.

## Replay rules

Every replay precondition failure yields exactly `{"error":"rejected"}` and changes **nothing**, including high-water counters and capacity. All successful operations below yield exactly `{"ok":true}` unless a richer result is specified. There is initially no active image and no objects. A stored context is `(epoch,state)`; its epoch is immutable and refers to a resident image. Advancing a context by a service uses that epoch's image, not the current active image. It does not alter its source. DENY is sticky. A newly created context consumes one context slot even when denied. A successful new request in a unit must have a `rid` strictly above that unit's high-water mark, initially zero. Finishing a request does not reset the mark. Existing contexts are immutable.

| op | exact fields besides op | successful effect/result |
|---|---|---|
| stage | epoch, policy | Compile and atomically install the image; return `{"ok":true,"epoch":E,"image":IMAGE}`. E must exceed every previously successful stage's epoch. Resident image/cell capacities apply; no partial map installation. |
| commit | epoch | Set the active pointer to any resident epoch. Previous images stay resident. Reactivation is allowed. |
| retire | epoch | Remove a resident, inactive image only when it has zero references. Successful stages' epoch high-water mark never decreases. |
| spawn | unit=U, service | Create a live unit at `(namespace,pid)` with this service, no contexts and request mark zero. No live unit may occupy that pair; generation must exceed its last successful spawn/clone generation, even after exit. |
| clone | parent=U, child=U | Parent must exist at that exact generation. Create child under the spawn identity/capacity rules, inheriting parent's service, request mark and a **by-value** copy of all contexts. Each copy consumes a context slot and image reference. No service is appended. |
| exit | unit=U | Remove that exact live unit and all its contexts. Packets and files survive. |
| begin | unit=U, rid | Active image and exact live unit required. Create `(active,START)` advanced once by the unit's service. Return `{"ok":true,"epoch":E,"state":S}`. |
| finish | unit=U, rid | Remove that existing context; return `{"ok":true,"allow":BOOL}`, using complete-path acceptance (false for DENY). |
| open | connection=C | Create a connection with no packets and stream mark zero. ID must not be open; generation must exceed its last successful open, even after close. |
| send | unit=U, rid, connection=C, stream, destination | Source context and exact open connection required. Stream must exceed that connection's mark. Retain a packet with the source context and destination, set the mark, consume one packet slot/reference and return `{"ok":true,"wire":HEX}` as specified below. Source context stays unchanged; denied contexts may be sent. |
| recv | connection=C, stream, unit=U, rid, wire | Packet must exist on the exact connection; unit service must equal its destination. null uses the retained bytes; explicit wire must be exactly the same 24 bytes encoded as 48 case-insensitive hex characters without spaces. First delivery creates a context advanced once by receiver service, records `(U,rid)` and returns its epoch/state. Later delivery succeeds only for that **same** `(U,rid)` while that exact context still exists, returns the same value, and appends nothing. Other duplicates reject, including after finish/exit. A duplicate does not consume capacity or raise the request mark. |
| close | connection=C | Remove exact open connection and all its packets/receipts, releasing packet references. Receiver contexts survive. |
| store | unit=U, rid, file=F | Snapshot source context into this inode/generation, consuming one file reference. With no current inode, generation must exceed its last successful store; capacity applies. With a current inode, only its **same** generation can be atomically overwritten, replacing its old reference. No service is appended. |
| load | file=F, unit=U, rid | Exact current file and unit required. Create a context from file's pinned epoch/state, advanced once by reader service; return its epoch/state. File is unchanged. This is an explicit observable last-writer handoff, not automatic inference or a merge of multiple causes. |
| unlink | file=F | Remove exact current file and release its reference; preserve generation high-water mark. |
| inspect | (none) | Return the snapshot below. |

Image references count **one per live context copy, retained packet, or current file**. Units, active pointers and receipts add no extra references. Successful `recv`/`load` create independent references. A packet continues to hold its reference after successful delivery. Generation checks apply to every operation carrying an identity. Request/stream/generation counters never wrap; an exhausted maximum cannot be incremented. Every insertion/clone/overwrite and capacity check is atomic. Images/contexts/units/etc. are per job, not shared between jobs.

Wire HEX is lowercase network byte order `4s, u32, u32, u32, u32, u32`: ASCII `EMC4`, epoch, source state (including DENY), numeric destination service label, stream ID, connection generation. Exactly 24 bytes/48 hex characters. The connection ID is supplied by the event and is not in these bytes. This is a modeled transport tag, not a cryptographic security guarantee.

`inspect` returns exactly `{"ok":true,"active":E_OR_NULL,"images":[[epoch,row_count,cell_count,reference_count],...],"units":N,"contexts":N,"connections":N,"packets":N,"files":N}`. Image entries are in increasing epoch order. Counts concern current resident objects, not historical generations. Every non-DENY row cell consumes one map cell; flags and DENY entries consume no map cells.

## Whole-request boundaries and execution limits

At most four jobs, 200000 total events, 16 total stage events, 8 MiB total UTF-8 policy strings, 32768 total atom occurrences and 65536 total path-service occurrences, counted over structurally valid jobs; each job has at most 200000 events. Invalid jobs do not contribute to whole-request totals. Policy occurrence counting follows the syntax paragraph above. Input is at most **24 MiB** (1 MiB=1048576 bytes). Artifact collection allows at most 8 MiB of ordinary files and 1024 entries including directories; symlinks, hardlinks and special files reject. Extra ordinary project files are allowed and counted. Generated bytecode may be disabled with `-B`; do not rely on mutable project paths at execution.

The control-plane work budget represents a two-minute CPU maintenance window for compiling a bounded registry batch and replaying its audit stream. The same whole request receives **120 CPU seconds soft/121 hard, 180 wall seconds, 2 GiB virtual address space, 32 FDs, no subprocesses or threads, 64 as the NPROC rlimit, 64 MiB per file, zero core size**, stdout at most 256 MiB and stderr at most 1 MiB. Stdout is captured through bounded pipes: its 256 MiB byte cap is separate from the 64 MiB regular-file limit. A verifier must not silently turn the pipe allowance into a smaller file allowance. The 2 GiB address-space allowance accommodates permitted bulk inspection responses and ordinary bulk JSON encoding; streaming is optional. No network. Only `/workspace/tmp` is writable during verification; project, packages and all other files are read-only. Scratch has a sampled 1 GiB/50000-entry emergency limit; this is not an attested hard aggregate quota. No process may remain after an invocation. No `/proc`, external files, an external build toolchain, devices beyond null/zero/random/urandom, credentials or private verifier data are available. Python standard library and the pinned FAdo 2.2.0/Lark 1.2.2 runtime closure at `/opt/emicro-deps` are supplied offline. No installation is required. The immutable local worker also includes basic shell utilities; they are not needed by this task.

The event and image bounds permit responses above 64 MiB. A legal 200000-event batch with 16 resident images and full u32 epochs has a compact response of 81597023 bytes (97396067 with default JSON separators). A conservative envelope that charges every event a maximal 16-image inspection and additionally allows all 16 maximal 8192-by-16 stage tables is at most 147522320 bytes compact, or 165550656 with default separators, below the 256 MiB cap. Arbitrary extra formatting whitespace still counts toward the cap. No event/image/path/state capacity is reduced by this output-budget repair.

Linux x86-64 syscall filtering kills wrong ABI/x32. It denies clone/fork/vfork/threads (clone3 reports ENOSYS), socket/socketpair/connect, System V shared-memory/semaphore/message-queue operations, kill/tkill/tgkill, ptrace/process-memory access, mount/umount/pivot_root/chroot, setsid/setpgid, setuid/setgid/setreuid/setregid/setresuid/setresgid/setgroups, BPF/perf, keyring, userfaultfd, io_uring, open_by_handle_at/name_to_handle_at, setns/unshare, and pidfd_getfd. Exact denied syscall numbers and rlimits are public in `child_guard.py`; the verification worker applies the same candidate profile. These restrictions are operational boundaries, not implementation requirements for a particular Python I/O style.

Run `python3 /workspace/public_check.py` as the image's nonroot user. It invokes actual bounded child CLI processes using only public files. It checks the small manual fixture and JSON transport/validation, not every lifecycle/scale family. Passing it is only a sanity check. The final verifier is separately bundled; no hidden tests/solutions are in this environment. Docker/Harbor production isolation and aggregate quota attestation are separate pending infrastructure gates, not local success claims.

"""Public child restrictions for Linux x86_64. No candidate imports in this process."""
import ctypes
import errno
import os
import platform
import resource

# x86_64 syscall numbers. Keep synchronized with PROTOCOL.md.
DENIED = (41,53,42,29,30,31,64,65,66,220,68,69,70,71,62,200,234,101,
          310,311,272,308,165,166,155,161,112,109,105,106,113,114,117,119,
          116,304,303,321,250,248,249,298,323,425,426,427,438,57,58,56)


def restrict():
    if os.geteuid() == 0 or platform.machine() != 'x86_64':
        raise RuntimeError('public checks require a nonprivileged Linux x86_64 process')
    for kind, soft, hard in ((resource.RLIMIT_AS, 2*1024**3, 2*1024**3),
                             (resource.RLIMIT_CPU,120,121),
                             (resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE,32,32),
                             (resource.RLIMIT_FSIZE,64*1024**2,64*1024**2),
                             (resource.RLIMIT_NPROC,64,64),
                             (resource.RLIMIT_CORE,0,0)):
        resource.setrlimit(kind, (soft, hard))
    class Filter(ctypes.Structure):
        _fields_ = [('code',ctypes.c_ushort),('jt',ctypes.c_ubyte),
                    ('jf',ctypes.c_ubyte),('k',ctypes.c_uint)]
    class Program(ctypes.Structure):
        _fields_ = [('length',ctypes.c_ushort),('filters',ctypes.POINTER(Filter))]
    statements = [(0x20,0,0,4),(0x15,1,0,0xC000003E),(0x06,0,0,0x80000000),
                  (0x20,0,0,0),(0x35,0,1,0x40000000),(0x06,0,0,0x80000000),
                  (0x15,0,1,435),(0x06,0,0,0x50000|errno.ENOSYS)]
    for number in DENIED:
        statements.extend([(0x15,0,1,number),(0x06,0,0,0x50000|errno.EPERM)])
    statements.append((0x06,0,0,0x7FFF0000))
    filters = (Filter*len(statements))(*(Filter(*s) for s in statements))
    program = Program(len(filters),filters)
    libc = ctypes.CDLL(None, use_errno=True)
    # prctl variadic arguments require pointer-sized explicit conversions.
    if libc.prctl(38,1,0,0,0) != 0:
        raise OSError(ctypes.get_errno(), 'no_new_privs')
    if libc.prctl(22,2,ctypes.byref(program),0,0) != 0:
        raise OSError(ctypes.get_errno(), 'seccomp')


def pidfd_open(pid):
    if hasattr(os,'pidfd_open'):
        return os.pidfd_open(pid)
    libc=ctypes.CDLL(None,use_errno=True)
    result=libc.syscall(434,pid,0)
    if result < 0:
        raise OSError(ctypes.get_errno(),'pidfd_open')
    return result


def pidfd_kill(fd):
    libc=ctypes.CDLL(None,use_errno=True)
    if libc.syscall(424,fd,9,0,0) < 0 and ctypes.get_errno() != errno.ESRCH:
        raise OSError(ctypes.get_errno(),'pidfd_send_signal')

    limits = job["limits"]
    events = job["events"]

            else:
                outcomes.append(agent.event(event))
        results.append({"events": outcomes})
    return {"results": results}

001: # eMicro offline control-plane contract, version 4.0.2
002: 
003: Repair and extend the supplied multi-file compiler and CPU map agent. The evaluated system compiles policies, publishes immutable map images, and replays explicit causal events. It models request identity and observable transport/storage handoffs; it does not run a kernel, deploy services, authenticate peers or infer causality from real traffic.
004: 
005: ## Artifact and command
006: 
007: The editable artifact is the **entire `/workspace/project` directory**, including any additional ordinary files you need. Implement its `driver.py`. All files in that directory are collected; no particular internal algorithm, class, module arrangement or coding style is required. The supplied compiler constructs real FAdo automata; the serial export and memory-map loader run on CPU. Their existing behavior is incomplete. The parser/JSON entry skeleton is supplied. In particular, the starter does not implement the required lifecycle, transactions or canonical export, and retains legacy language/empty-language/performance defects.
008: 
009: `python3 /workspace/launch.py` runs `project/driver.py` with the pinned offline packages on its import path, working directory `/workspace/project`. Read one UTF-8 JSON request from stdin, write one JSON response to stdout and exit **0**. JSON key order/whitespace do not matter. Array order, integer values and Boolean types do. Extra stdout, empty/non-JSON output, wrong values or nonzero exit fail. Stderr is diagnostic only. No Python stream interception is used. Text, binary streams and OS descriptors 0/1 all work. Flushed valid output followed by `os._exit(0)` is accepted. Each invocation has fresh system state; jobs are independent.
010: 
011: The request is exactly `{"jobs":[JOB,...]}`. A job has exactly `services`, `limits`, `events`. The response is exactly `{"results":[RESULT,...]}`. A valid job yields `{"events":[OUTCOME,...]}` in event order. Invalid job structure/types/static bounds yield `{"error":"invalid"}` for that job, with no replay. Invalid UTF-8/JSON, duplicate keys, nonfinite numbers, incorrect top-level schema or whole-request bounds yield `{"error":"invalid"}` for the whole request. JSON floating-point tokens are decoded to binary64; a token that overflows to infinity is a whole-request error, while underflow to finite zero is permitted. Finite JSON floats are parsed but never valid for integer fields; Booleans are not integers. Trailing whitespace is allowed; trailing JSON is not. Integer tokens longer than 4300 decimal digits (excluding a leading minus) are whole-request JSON errors. JSON container nesting is limited to 64: each object or array contributes one level, including the outer request object at level 1; strings, including escaped brackets/quotes, contribute none. Exceeding 64 levels is a whole-request `invalid` error before job validation, even when the deep value is in an otherwise invalid job. Up to 64 levels, malformed job contents retain job-level error scope. Malformed JSON and parser failures are whole-request errors, never partial results. A leading UTF-8 BOM is rejected. JSON whitespace outside strings is exactly space U+0020, tab U+0009, LF U+000A and CR U+000D.
012: 
013: `services` is a nonempty list of at most 16 objects exactly `{"name":NAME,"label":LABEL}`. Names match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,23}` and labels are integers 1..4294967294; both are unique. Every image uses columns in **increasing label order**, independent of registry order. `limits` has exactly these keys, each an integer from 1 to the shown maximum:
014: 
015: | key | maximum | resident objects counted |
016: |---|---:|---|
017: | images | 16 | staged/active/inactive immutable images |
018: | cells | 262144 | transitions whose target is not DENY, across resident images |
019: | units | 1024 | live process identities |
020: | contexts | 32768 | all live request contexts, including cloned copies |
021: | connections | 4096 | open connection generations |
022: | packets | 32768 | sent packets retained until close, including delivered packets |
023: | files | 8192 | current inode generations |
024: 
025: An event is an object with exactly `op` and the fields listed below. `U` means `[namespace,pid,generation]`, with namespace 0..4294967295 and the other two fields 1..4294967295. `C` and `F` mean `[id,generation]`, both fields 1..4294967295. All epochs, request IDs (`rid`) and stream IDs are integers 1..4294967295. Services/destinations must have the NAME lexical form; an unregistered one is a replay rejection. `policy` is a UTF-8-encodable string; an unpaired surrogate makes that job invalid. There is **no separate per-string byte cap**. The 8 MiB policy-byte budget is exclusively a whole-request sum over structurally valid jobs, including strings whose policy grammar or replay stage is rejected. Thus an otherwise valid job containing one string longer than 8 MiB causes whole-request `invalid`; a structurally invalid job is excluded from that sum. The 24 MiB raw-input cap still includes all jobs and bytes. `wire` is null or a string of at most 96 characters; malformed contents cause a replay rejection. Unknown operations/fields, missing fields and incorrect types make the **job** invalid.
026: 
027: ## Policy language and images
028: 
029: A policy string is zero or more `PREDICATE ACTION;` rules; the only ignored whitespace between tokens is space U+0020, tab U+0009, form feed U+000C, CR U+000D and LF U+000A. Vertical tab U+000B and all other Unicode whitespace are forbidden in policy syntax and reject that `stage`; characters within a service name are never ignored. ACTION is `allow` or `drop`. Predicates are `match(PATH)`, `startswith(PATH)`, `endswith(PATH)`, `contains(PATH)`, `(PREDICATE and PREDICATE)`, `(PREDICATE or PREDICATE)` or `not(PREDICATE)`. PATH is a comma-separated sequence of registered names, possibly empty. Parentheses in binary expressions are mandatory. No comments/other syntax is supported. Predicates concern sequences of **services**, not characters. `match` is exact equality; the other three are prefix, suffix and contiguous subsequence. Empty paths match every sequence for those three and only the empty sequence for `match`. Boolean operations have their usual set meanings over every finite sequence of registered services. A sequence is allowed iff at least one allow rule matches and no drop rule matches. No allow rules means the empty language.
030: 
031: Each rule has predicate nesting depth at most 16 (an atom has depth 1), every path has at most 16 services. At most eight rules per string may have a predicate other than a single `match` atom; each such predicate has at most 32 atom occurrences. There are at most four **distinct** non-`match` atoms per string, each with path length at most four. Each string has at most 32768 atom occurrences and 65536 path-service occurrences. Syntax/registry/these policy-bound violations reject that `stage` event. A syntactically valid string satisfying these bounds is counted toward the whole-request atom/path totals even if it names an unregistered service or its stage is later rejected. Invalid strings are not counted toward these two totals.
032: 
033: An image is exactly `{"accept":[BOOL,...],"rows":[[TARGET,...],...]}`. It represents the minimal deterministic complete language machine after removal of its dead residual. Two histories share a label exactly when every possible continuation has the same allowedness. Label 0 is the empty history's residual, called START. Retain only residuals that can reach an allowed sequence, except START is always retained. All other/dead transitions have the integer target **DENY=4294967295**. DENY has no row and remains DENY under every service. Number the retained residuals by breadth-first discovery from START, considering outgoing columns in increasing service-label order and ignoring DENY. `accept[s]` is allowedness of a complete history with label `s`; live-prefix reachability does not imply acceptance. An empty language has one false acceptance flag and one all-DENY row. An all-allow language has one true flag and a row of zeroes. Reject a stage whose resulting image has more than 8192 rows. These are output semantics, not an implementation prescription.
034: 
035: ## Replay rules
036: 
037: Every replay precondition failure yields exactly `{"error":"rejected"}` and changes **nothing**, including high-water counters and capacity. All successful operations below yield exactly `{"ok":true}` unless a richer result is specified. There is initially no active image and no objects. A stored context is `(epoch,state)`; its epoch is immutable and refers to a resident image. Advancing a context by a service uses that epoch's image, not the current active image. It does not alter its source. DENY is sticky. A newly created context consumes one context slot even when denied. A successful new request in a unit must have a `rid` strictly above that unit's high-water mark, initially zero. Finishing a request does not reset the mark. Existing contexts are immutable.
038: 
039: | op | exact fields besides op | successful effect/result |
040: |---|---|---|
041: | stage | epoch, policy | Compile and atomically install the image; return `{"ok":true,"epoch":E,"image":IMAGE}`. E must exceed every previously successful stage's epoch. Resident image/cell capacities apply; no partial map installation. |
042: | commit | epoch | Set the active pointer to any resident epoch. Previous images stay resident. Reactivation is allowed. |
043: | retire | epoch | Remove a resident, inactive image only when it has zero references. Successful stages' epoch high-water mark never decreases. |
044: | spawn | unit=U, service | Create a live unit at `(namespace,pid)` with this service, no contexts and request mark zero. No live unit may occupy that pair; generation must exceed its last successful spawn/clone generation, even after exit. |
045: | clone | parent=U, child=U | Parent must exist at that exact generation. Create child under the spawn identity/capacity rules, inheriting parent's service, request mark and a **by-value** copy of all contexts. Each copy consumes a context slot and image reference. No service is appended. |
046: | exit | unit=U | Remove that exact live unit and all its contexts. Packets and files survive. |
047: | begin | unit=U, rid | Active image and exact live unit required. Create `(active,START)` advanced once by the unit's service. Return `{"ok":true,"epoch":E,"state":S}`. |
048: | finish | unit=U, rid | Remove that existing context; return `{"ok":true,"allow":BOOL}`, using complete-path acceptance (false for DENY). |
049: | open | connection=C | Create a connection with no packets and stream mark zero. ID must not be open; generation must exceed its last successful open, even after close. |
050: | send | unit=U, rid, connection=C, stream, destination | Source context and exact open connection required. Stream must exceed that connection's mark. Retain a packet with the source context and destination, set the mark, consume one packet slot/reference and return `{"ok":true,"wire":HEX}` as specified below. Source context stays unchanged; denied contexts may be sent. |
051: | recv | connection=C, stream, unit=U, rid, wire | Packet must exist on the exact connection; unit service must equal its destination. null uses the retained bytes; explicit wire must be exactly the same 24 bytes encoded as 48 case-insensitive hex characters without spaces. First delivery creates a context advanced once by receiver service, records `(U,rid)` and returns its epoch/state. Later delivery succeeds only for that **same** `(U,rid)` while that exact context still exists, returns the same value, and appends nothing. Other duplicates reject, including after finish/exit. A duplicate does not consume capacity or raise the request mark. |
052: | close | connection=C | Remove exact open connection and all its packets/receipts, releasing packet references. Receiver contexts survive. |
053: | store | unit=U, rid, file=F | Snapshot source context into this inode/generation, consuming one file reference. With no current inode, generation must exceed its last successful store; capacity applies. With a current inode, only its **same** generation can be atomically overwritten, replacing its old reference. No service is appended. |
054: | load | file=F, unit=U, rid | Exact current file and unit required. Create a context from file's pinned epoch/state, advanced once by reader service; return its epoch/state. File is unchanged. This is an explicit observable last-writer handoff, not automatic inference or a merge of multiple causes. |
055: | unlink | file=F | Remove exact current file and release its reference; preserve generation high-water mark. |
056: | inspect | (none) | Return the snapshot below. |
057: 
058: Image references count **one per live context copy, retained packet, or current file**. Units, active pointers and receipts add no extra references. Successful `recv`/`load` create independent references. A packet continues to hold its reference after successful delivery. Generation checks apply to every operation carrying an identity. Request/stream/generation counters never wrap; an exhausted maximum cannot be incremented. Every insertion/clone/overwrite and capacity check is atomic. Images/contexts/units/etc. are per job, not shared between jobs.
059: 
060: Wire HEX is lowercase network byte order `4s, u32, u32, u32, u32, u32`: ASCII `EMC4`, epoch, source state (including DENY), numeric destination service label, stream ID, connection generation. Exactly 24 bytes/48 hex characters. The connection ID is supplied by the event and is not in these bytes. This is a modeled transport tag, not a cryptographic security guarantee.
061: 
062: `inspect` returns exactly `{"ok":true,"active":E_OR_NULL,"images":[[epoch,row_count,cell_count,reference_count],...],"units":N,"contexts":N,"connections":N,"packets":N,"files":N}`. Image entries are in increasing epoch order. Counts concern current resident objects, not historical generations. Every non-DENY row cell consumes one map cell; flags and DENY entries consume no map cells.
063: 
064: ## Whole-request boundaries and execution limits
065: 
066: At most four jobs, 200000 total events, 16 total stage events, 8 MiB total UTF-8 policy strings, 32768 total atom occurrences and 65536 total path-service occurrences, counted over structurally valid jobs; each job has at most 200000 events. Invalid jobs do not contribute to whole-request totals. Policy occurrence counting follows the syntax paragraph above. Input is at most **24 MiB** (1 MiB=1048576 bytes). Artifact collection allows at most 8 MiB of ordinary files and 1024 entries including directories; symlinks, hardlinks and special files reject. Extra ordinary project files are allowed and counted. Generated bytecode may be disabled with `-B`; do not rely on mutable project paths at execution.
067: 
068: The control-plane work budget represents a two-minute CPU maintenance window for compiling a bounded registry batch and replaying its audit stream. The same whole request receives **120 CPU seconds soft/121 hard, 180 wall seconds, 2 GiB virtual address space, 32 FDs, no subprocesses or threads, 64 as the NPROC rlimit, 64 MiB per file, zero core size**, stdout at most 256 MiB and stderr at most 1 MiB. Stdout is captured through bounded pipes: its 256 MiB byte cap is separate from the 64 MiB regular-file limit. A verifier must not silently turn the pipe allowance into a smaller file allowance. The 2 GiB address-space allowance accommodates permitted bulk inspection responses and ordinary bulk JSON encoding; streaming is optional. No network. Only `/workspace/tmp` is writable during verification; project, packages and all other files are read-only. Scratch has a sampled 1 GiB/50000-entry emergency limit; this is not an attested hard aggregate quota. No process may remain after an invocation. No `/proc`, external files, an external build toolchain, devices beyond null/zero/random/urandom, credentials or private verifier data are available. Python standard library and the pinned FAdo 2.2.0/Lark 1.2.2 runtime closure at `/opt/emicro-deps` are supplied offline. No installation is required. The immutable local worker also includes basic shell utilities; they are not needed by this task.
069: 
070: The event and image bounds permit responses above 64 MiB. A legal 200000-event batch with 16 resident images and full u32 epochs has a compact response of 81597023 bytes (97396067 with default JSON separators). A conservative envelope that charges every event a maximal 16-image inspection and additionally allows all 16 maximal 8192-by-16 stage tables is at most 147522320 bytes compact, or 165550656 with default separators, below the 256 MiB cap. Arbitrary extra formatting whitespace still counts toward the cap. No event/image/path/state capacity is reduced by this output-budget repair.
071: 
072: Linux x86-64 syscall filtering kills wrong ABI/x32. It denies clone/fork/vfork/threads (clone3 reports ENOSYS), socket/socketpair/connect, System V shared-memory/semaphore/message-queue operations, kill/tkill/tgkill, ptrace/process-memory access, mount/umount/pivot_root/chroot, setsid/setpgid, setuid/setgid/setreuid/setregid/setresuid/setresgid/setgroups, BPF/perf, keyring, userfaultfd, io_uring, open_by_handle_at/name_to_handle_at, setns/unshare, and pidfd_getfd. Exact denied syscall numbers and rlimits are public in `child_guard.py`; the verification worker applies the same candidate profile. These restrictions are operational boundaries, not implementation requirements for a particular Python I/O style.
073: 
074: Run `python3 /workspace/public_check.py` as the image's nonroot user. It invokes actual bounded child CLI processes using only public files. It checks the small manual fixture and JSON transport/validation, not every lifecycle/scale family. Passing it is only a sanity check. The final verifier is separately bundled; no hidden tests/solutions are in this environment. Docker/Harbor production isolation and aggregate quota attestation are separate pending infrastructure gates, not local success claims.

not the current active image. It does not alter its source. DENY is sticky. A newly created context consumes one context slot even when denied. A
successful new request in a unit must have a `rid` strictly above that unit's high-water mark, initially zero. Finishing a request does not reset the
mark. Existing contexts are immutable.

39 | op | exact fields besides op | successful effect/result |
40 |---|---|---|
41 | stage | epoch, policy | Compile and atomically install the image; return `{"ok":true,"epoch":E,"image":IMAGE}`. E must exceed every previously
successful stage's epoch. Resident image/cell capacities apply; no partial map installation. |
42 | commit | epoch | Set the active pointer to any resident epoch. Previous images stay resident. Reactivation is allowed. |
43 | retire | epoch | Remove a resident, inactive image only when it has zero references. Successful stages' epoch high-water mark never decreases. |
44 | spawn | unit=U, service | Create a live unit at `(namespace,pid)` with this service, no contexts and request mark zero. No live unit may occupy that
pair; generation must exceed its last successful spawn/clone generation, even after exit. |
45 | clone | parent=U, child=U | Parent must exist at that exact generation. Create child under the spawn identity/capacity rules, inheriting parent's
service, request mark and a **by-value** copy of all contexts. Each copy consumes a context slot and image reference. No service is appended. |
46 | exit | unit=U | Remove that exact live unit and all its contexts. Packets and files survive. |
47 | begin | unit=U, rid | Active image and exact live unit required. Create `(active,START)` advanced once by the unit's service. Return
`{"ok":true,"epoch":E,"state":S}`. |
48 | finish | unit=U, rid | Remove that existing context; return `{"ok":true,"allow":BOOL}`, using complete-path acceptance (false for DENY). |
49 | open | connection=C | Create a connection with no packets and stream mark zero. ID must not be open; generation must exceed its last successful
open, even after close. |
50 | send | unit=U, rid, connection=C, stream, destination | Source context and exact open connection required. Stream must exceed that connection's
mark. Retain a packet with the source context and destination, set the mark, consume one packet slot/reference and return `{"ok":true,"wire":HEX}` as
specified below. Source context stays unchanged; denied contexts may be sent. |
51 | recv | connection=C, stream, unit=U, rid, wire | Packet must exist on the exact connection; unit service must equal its destination. null uses the
retained bytes; explicit wire must be exactly the same 24 bytes encoded as 48 case-insensitive hex characters without spaces. First delivery creates a
context advanced once by receiver service, records `(U,rid)` and returns its epoch/state. Later delivery succeeds only for that **same** `(U,rid)`
while that exact context still exists, returns the same value, and appends nothing. Other duplicates reject, including after finish/exit. A duplicate
does not consume capacity or raise the request mark. |
52 | close | connection=C | Remove exact open connection and all its packets/receipts, releasing packet references. Receiver contexts survive. |
53 | store | unit=U, rid, file=F | Snapshot source context into this inode/generation, consuming one file reference. With no current inode, generation
must exceed its last successful store; capacity applies. With a current inode, only its **same** generation can be atomically overwritten, replacing
its old reference. No service is appended. |
54 | load | file=F, unit=U, rid | Exact current file and unit required. Create a context from file's pinned epoch/state, advanced once by reader service;
return its epoch/state. File is unchanged. This is an explicit observable last-writer handoff, not automatic inference or a merge of multiple causes.
|
55 | unlink | file=F | Remove exact current file and release its reference; preserve generation high-water mark. |
56 | inspect | (none) | Return the snapshot below. |

Successful `recv`/`load` create independent references. A packet continues to hold its reference after successful delivery. Generation checks apply to
